about: The scoped term-ruling set the AI-reviewed layer's gate reads (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-ai-layer-scaffolding-design.md, Unit B). Compiled by tools/ai-review/compile-ruling-set.js from `base` (the frozen 2026-10-11 set: its stage1 and before rows) and `exceptions` (scope exceptions to D2's book-wide default). Deterministic: a test recompiles it and requires byte equality, so never edit it by hand. One ruling per enNorm, after the base's supersededInBefore is applied (a superseded target survives only as a competitor). `id` is a slug of enNorm minted here. `en` lists every English form the rows carry, plus each form with its parentheticals removed (case kept). `is` is the recorded target, unchanged. `competitors` are the other renderings the rows name: a before row's competitor; a stage1 row's stored word, tied words, stored alternatives and superseded page answer; any superseded target; never the target itself. `kinds` are the before kinds plus 'stage1'; `sources` cite each row. `scope` is {kind:'book'} with scopeStatus 'default' unless the exceptions file names the headword; a 'proposed' width is not ruled, and the gate admits no operation for it. `matchable` is false, with codes in unmatchableReason, when the target holds a digit, a Greek letter, an uppercase letter after the first letter of a run of letters, an operator or bracket character, an underscore, or a non-ASCII space or control character, or when the enNorm holds a bracketed placeholder such as [formula]. Held rows and rows without a target are listed under `excluded`, never ruled.

rulings.enNorm: bohr’s model of the hydrogen atom
en: Bohr’s model of the hydrogen atom

rulings.enNorm: standard conditions of temperature and pressure
en: standard conditions of temperature and pressure
standard conditions of temperature and pressure (STP)

rulings.is: kenningin um fráhrindingu rafeindapara í gildishvolfi

notes.text: matchable checks the target's characters and the enNorm's placeholders only. It does not check element-symbol words (the gate's lexicon owns ELEMENT_SYMBOLS) or whether an English form occurs in visible prose; the gate checks both per operation.

notes.source: server/lib/houseStyleTerms.js line 210 at commit 6cbd36ed0: the why of the cell entry (lines 206-211), "SEND IT IN ch17's SUBSET ONLY". The class of exception was ruled by D2, docs/decisions/2026-10-11-chemistry-finish-preparation-answers.md line 43; the chapter was not.
notes.note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED. ch17 is an MT-wire note: it says which chapter's --glossary-only subset carries the row, not where the ruling applies. The width awaits [USER]'s ruling. A chapter list does not separate the senses: the electrochemical cell also occurs in ch01, ch11, ch18, ch19 and the appendices (spec 2026-10-26, measured inputs), while a biological cell is another sense and ch10's unit cell is a separate term. A raw word-bounded count of cell/cells over the 02-for-mt EN segment files on 2026-10-26 found the word in 21 of 23 chapter directories (ch17 376, ch10 142, ch03 64). That count includes marker payloads such as E[[sub:cell]] and compounds such as unit cell, so it over-counts and does not separate senses.
